# RolePatch

> Evidence-bound resume tailoring for a serious application to one specific job. RolePatch may reframe supplied proof, but it must not invent a skill, metric, employer, tool, or accomplishment.

## When to use RolePatch

- Matching a job description against a base resume, project stash, and achievement evidence
- Reviewing a proposed resume patch in a word-level diff before accepting it
- Preparing a cover letter, fit analysis, interview stories, and an application packet from the same supplied proof
- Queueing a job, filling supported ATS fields after review, and keeping blocked, failed, or successful receipts

## Do not use RolePatch for

- Inventing qualifications or closing an unsupported requirement with fabricated evidence
- Predicting a universal hiring outcome from a fit score
- Unattended bulk submission, CAPTCHA bypass, or automatic file upload

## Access and pricing

- Guest records can stay in the current browser; clearing browser storage can remove them
- Google sign-in adds user-scoped account persistence and three starting tokens
- Signed-in AI operations use tokens; implemented packs are 10 for $5, 30 for $12, and 100 for $30
- Public ATS, keyword, bullet, diff, snippet, and word-count tools work without sign-up

## Public surfaces

- [Home](https://rolepatch.com/) — product purpose, evidence rule, access, and safety boundaries
- [Pricing](https://rolepatch.com/pricing) — exact token packs and access model
- [Free tools](https://rolepatch.com/tools) — browser-based resume checks
- [FAQ](https://rolepatch.com/faq) — storage, pricing, extension, and product-state answers
- [Public catalog](https://rolepatch.com/api/ai) — every indexed HTML and Markdown surface
- [OpenAPI](https://rolepatch.com/openapi.json) — read-only machine-surface description
- [Product brief](https://rolepatch.com/index.md) — canonical Markdown summary

User-specific dashboard and API routes are not public agent surfaces.
